title: Fact Families and Leftovers
goal: I can write all the facts in a fact family and tell what is left over when things don't share evenly.

card.desc: Bailey turns each fact triangle into a full fact family (two multiplication facts, two division facts), finds the families with only two facts, and learns which facts do not belong. Then she meets remainders with small numbers like 30 ÷ 7 by dealing beans into cups, plus seven new words. The after-class lesson has her do it all on her own.

win: Fact families and leftovers: you handled both like a pro!

slides.title: On Your Own: Fact Families and Leftovers
slides.text: In class you built fact families and dealt beans into cups. Now you do it on your own. It takes about 25 minutes and ends with Show What You Know.

slides.title: Teach it to someone
slides.text: Find someone at home. Teach them. Say it out loud before you go on.
prompts: Show them the 6, 8, 48 family. Say all four facts.
Explain why the 7, 7, 49 family has only two facts.
Explain a remainder with 30 fish and 7 dragons. Why can't the 2 extra fish be shared?
starters: It has only two facts because …
Each dragon gets … and … are left because …

slides.title: Remember the words
slides.text: Tap each card. Say the meaning before you flip it. Then flip to check yourself.

words.meaning: A set of related multiplication and division facts made from the same three numbers.
The amount left over when a number cannot be split into equal groups.
In equal parts, with nothing left over.
An extra amount, more than what is needed.
words.example: After every dragon was fed, there was a surplus of 3 fish.

words.meaning: Hard to find because there is very little of it.
words.example: In the middle of winter, fresh food was scarce.

words.meaning: To stop or wait for a moment before doing something, because you are unsure.
words.example: Do not hesitate: if you know 7 × 8 = 56, you know 56 ÷ 8.

words.meaning: To talk with someone to reach an agreement.
words.example: Instead of fighting, the two tribes agreed to negotiate.

slides.title: Two big ideas
slides.text: A fact family is all the × and ÷ facts made from three numbers. A remainder is what is left when things do not share evenly.

steps.text: Leftovers: find the biggest fact that fits, subtract, and check that the remainder is smaller than the divisor.

items.no: Which number has not been the answer yet?

items.q: How many different facts are in the 6, 6, 36 family? Type a number.
items.why: 6 × 6 = 36 and 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Turning them around gives the same facts.
items.no: Write them. Are any the same?

items.q: What number is missing from this fact triangle? Type it.
items.no: Ask: 9 × what = 63?

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the 7, 8, 56 family?
items.why: 8 ÷ 56 is backward. In division the biggest number comes first.
no: That one uses 7, 8 and 56, and it is true.
The turn-around fact belongs.
That one uses 7, 8 and 56, and it is true.

slides.title: The 7, 8, 56 family
slides.text: Tap a fact. Does it belong in the 7, 8, 56 fact family?

items.why: Uses 7, 8 and 56, and it is true.
items.hint: Which three numbers? Is it true?

items.why: 8 × 6 = 48, not 56. A false fact is not in any family.
Same three numbers, and it is true.
Backward. In division the biggest number comes first.
items.hint: Which number should come first in division?

items.why: 65 is not 56. The digits got switched, and the fact is not true either.
items.hint: Read the first number carefully: 65 or 56?

items.why: The turn-around fact belongs too.
items.hint: Does turning it around change the numbers?

items.why: Subtraction is not in a multiplication and division family.
items.hint: Which operations are in a fact family?

slides.done: A fact belongs only if it uses the same three numbers, the right operation, AND it is true.

slides.title: Toothless shares his catch
slides.text: Toothless caught 31 fish for 7 dragons. Every dragon gets the same number, as many as possible. Make the groups.
slides.why: 7 × 4 = 28 fish handed out. 31 − 28 = 3 left over. So 31 ÷ 7 = 4 R 3.
slides.hint: 7 dragons means 7 groups. Is 7 × 5 = 35 more than 31? Then each dragon gets fewer than 5.

slides.title: Leftovers
slides.text: Type the answer with R for the remainder, like 4 R 2.

items.no: Find the biggest 9s fact that fits under 52 without going over.
Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 44 without going over.

items.q: Stoick has 40 arrows for 6 archers. Each archer gets the same number. How many arrows are left over?
items.why: 6 × 6 = 36 and 40 − 36 = 4. So 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4: 4 arrows left over.
items.no: Find the biggest 6s fact under 40 first.

items.q: Which division has a remainder?
no: 9 × 4 = 36 exactly.
7 × 6 = 42 exactly.
6 × 8 = 48 exactly.

slides.title: Steps for 47 ÷ 6
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
steps: Ask: 6 × what gets close to 47 without going over?
Check: 5 is smaller than 6, so no more groups fit
slides.why: Find the biggest fact that fits, subtract, check the remainder, then write it.
slides.hint: You need the fact before you can subtract. What comes first?

slides.title: Words in action
slides.text: Type the word.

items.q: After every dragon was fed, there were 5 extra fish. There was a ____ of fish. (Use a word from your word cards.)
items.why: A surplus is an extra amount, more than what is needed.
items.no: It means extra. It is the opposite of scarce.

items.q: 54 beans split into 6 cups with nothing left over. They split ____.
items.why: Evenly means in equal parts with nothing left over.
items.no: It ends in -ly.

items.q: The two tribes sat down to negotiate. What did they do?
items.why: To negotiate is to talk with someone to reach an agreement.
no: Running away is not talking it out.
Negotiating is what you do INSTEAD of fighting.

items.q: In 63 ÷ 9 = 7, the 9 is called the ____.
items.why: The divisor is the number you divide by.
items.no: It is the number you divide BY.
Ask: 8 × what = 48?

sets.q: Which fact is in the same family as 3 × 9 = 27?
sets.why: 27 ÷ 9 = 3 uses the same three numbers: 3, 9 and 27.
no: True, but 36 and 4 are not in this family.
Backward. The biggest number comes first.
Subtraction is not in a multiplication and division family.

sets.q: Which number is missing from this fact triangle? Type it.
Which list is the complete fact family for 6, 7 and 42?
sets.why: Two multiplication facts and two division facts, all using 6, 7 and 42.
no: 6 ÷ 42 is backward.
Adding and subtracting are not in this family.
49 belongs to a different family.

sets.q: 30 ÷ 8 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 30 without going over.

sets.q: 41 ÷ 6 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 6s fact that fits under 41 without going over.

sets.q: Stoick has 33 arrows for 8 archers. Each archer gets the same number. What is 33 ÷ 8? Use R for what is left.
sets.no: Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 33 without going over.

sets.q: Which remainder is impossible when you divide by 7?
sets.why: A remainder must be smaller than the divisor. With 8 left over, another group of 7 fits.
no: 0 is possible: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 has no remainder.
3 is possible: 24 ÷ 7 = 3 R 3.
6 is possible: 20 ÷ 7 = 2 R 6.

sets.q: Related × and ÷ facts made from the same three numbers are called a fact ____.
sets.why: A fact family uses one set of three numbers, like 6, 8 and 48.
sets.no: Three numbers, four facts, like parents and kids.

sets.q: The amount left over after dividing is called the ____.
sets.why: The remainder is the part left over.
sets.no: On paper we write just its first letter: R.

sets.q: Hiccup did not hesitate: he jumped on Toothless right away. What does hesitate mean?
choices: to stop for a moment because you are unsure
sets.why: To hesitate is to stop or wait for a moment because you are unsure.
no: Shouting is not stopping to think.
That is the opposite of hesitating.
Agreeing is not stopping to think.

sets.q: Which fact is in the same family as 8 × 4 = 32?
sets.why: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 uses the same three numbers: 4, 8 and 32.
no: Backward. The biggest number comes first.
Subtraction is not in this family.
That uses 5 and 40, a different family.

sets.q: What number goes in the empty corner of this fact triangle? Type it.

sets.no: Which number has not been the answer yet?

sets.q: 50 ÷ 7 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 7s fact that fits under 50 without going over.

sets.q: 35 ÷ 9 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 9s fact that fits under 35 without going over.

sets.q: Hiccup has 46 fish for 8 dragons. Each dragon gets the same number. How many fish are left over?
sets.why: 8 × 5 = 40 and 46 − 40 = 6. So 46 ÷ 8 = 5 R 6: 6 fish left over.
sets.no: Find the biggest 8s fact under 46 first.

sets.q: Fishlegs says 61 ÷ 9 = 5 R 16. What is wrong?
choices: 16 left over is enough for another group of 9. It should be 6 R 7.
no: The math adds up, but a remainder can never be as big as the divisor.
Adding makes more. This is a division problem.
9 × 6 = 54, so 7 are left over, not 0.

sets.q: When things split into equal parts with nothing left over, they split ____.
sets.why: Evenly means in equal parts, with nothing left over.

sets.q: Which division has no remainder?
sets.why: 6 × 4 = 24 exactly, so nothing is left over.
no: 8 × 7 = 56, so 2 are left over.
6 × 8 = 48, so 2 are left over.
7 × 8 = 56, so 6 are left over.

sets.q: After the feast, there was a surplus of bread. What does that mean?
choices: There was extra bread, more than needed.
sets.why: A surplus is an extra amount, more than what is needed.
no: That is scarce, the opposite of surplus.
If it was all eaten, nothing is extra.
Surplus tells how much, not how it was shared.

sets.q: Which list is the complete fact family for 4, 9 and 36?
sets.why: All four facts use only 4, 9 and 36.
no: 4 ÷ 36 is backward.
Adding and subtracting are not in this family.
81 belongs to a different family.

sets.q: What number is missing from this fact triangle? Type it.
sets.why: 8 × 5 = 40, so 40 ÷ 8 = 5. The family is 5, 8 and 40.

sets.no: Which number has not been the answer yet?

sets.q: 59 ÷ 8 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 59 without going over.

sets.q: 44 ÷ 9 = ____   (use R for the remainder)
sets.no: Find the biggest 9s fact that fits under 44 without going over.

sets.q: Stoick has 39 shields for 6 ships. Each ship gets the same number. Which answer is right?
no: 9 left over is more than 6. Each ship can get one more.
6 × 7 = 42. That is more shields than he has.
33 is 39 − 6. That is subtracting, not dividing.

sets.q: When you divide by 9, which remainder is impossible?
sets.why: A remainder must be smaller than the divisor. With 9 left over, one more group of 9 fits.
no: 8 is possible: 17 ÷ 9 = 1 R 8.
0 is possible: 63 ÷ 9 = 7 has no remainder.
5 is possible: 32 ÷ 9 = 3 R 5.

sets.q: Fresh fish were very hard to find in winter. Fish were ____. (Use a word from your word cards.)
sets.why: Scarce means hard to find because there is very little of it.
sets.no: It is the opposite of surplus.

sets.q: To talk together until you reach an agreement is to ____. (Use a word from your word cards.)
sets.why: To negotiate is to talk with someone to reach an agreement.
sets.no: Tribes do it instead of fighting. It starts with n.

sets.q: Which division has a remainder?
no: 9 × 6 = 54 exactly.
7 × 8 = 56 exactly.
8 × 8 = 64 exactly.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one, but only your first try counts. For leftovers, find the biggest fact that fits first. Type remainders like 4 R 2.

questions.q: Which fact is NOT in the 8, 9, 72 family?
questions.why: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 is true, but it uses 6 and 12. They are not in the 8, 9, 72 family.
no: That one uses 8, 9 and 72, so it belongs.
The turn-around fact belongs.
That one uses 8, 9 and 72, so it belongs.

questions.no: Which number has not been the answer yet?

questions.q: What is the missing number in this fact triangle? Type it.
How many different facts are in the 8, 8, 64 family? Type a number.

questions.no: Find the biggest 6s fact that fits under 20 without going over.
Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 47 without going over.

questions.q: Hiccup has 29 cod to share equally among 9 dragons. How many cod are left over?
questions.why: 9 × 3 = 27 and 29 − 27 = 2. So 29 ÷ 9 = 3 R 2: 2 cod left over.
questions.no: Find the biggest 9s fact under 29 first.

no: 7 × 5 = 35 exactly.
9 × 3 = 27 exactly.
8 × 4 = 32 exactly.

questions.q: What does evenly mean in "42 splits evenly into 7 groups"?
choices: in equal parts with nothing left over
questions.why: 7 × 6 = 42 exactly, so the groups are equal with nothing left.
no: That is not what evenly means in math.
That is the opposite.
Evenly is not about even numbers.
Surplus is extra, the opposite of scarce.
Scarce tells how much there was, not how it was shared.
With scarce food, a feast is unlikely.

questions.q: Which word means "to talk together to reach an agreement"? (Use a word from your word cards.)
questions.why: To negotiate is to talk until you agree.

questions.q: Fishlegs wrote 34 ÷ 6 = 4 R 10. Which is the right answer?
no: That is his answer. 10 left over is more than 6, so one more group fits.
6 × 6 = 36. That is more than 34.
6 × 5 = 30. You forgot the 4 left over.

pages.directions: Draw a line from each word to its meaning.

items.text: 1. Match each word to its meaning.

to stop for a moment because you are unsure
the amount left over after dividing
related facts made from the same three numbers
an extra amount, more than needed
in equal parts, nothing left over

pages.title: Part 2: Fact families
pages.directions: Write all the facts in each family. Two multiplication facts, then two division facts.

items.text: 4. The 9, 9, 81 family. Careful: how many different facts are there?

items.text: 10. Stoick has 53 shields for 9 ships. Each ship gets the same number. How many shields go on each ship? How many are left over?
11. Use surplus and remainder to tell about sharing food on Berk.
12. Tell about a time someone in your book had to hesitate. Why did they stop?

teacher.objective: Bailey writes all four facts in a fact family for the 6–9 facts (and knows a square like 7, 7, 49 has only two), spots facts that do not belong, and divides with a small leftover: finds the biggest fact that fits, subtracts, and writes the answer as a remainder (30 ÷ 7 = 4 R 2), knowing the remainder must be smaller than the divisor.
materials: Class lesson on your laptop or tablet (teacher code 9110)
Index cards: her three triangle cards from Lesson 9 plus 5 blank cards
Her book, How to Train Your Dragon
Packet (2 pages): page 1 due Thursday, page 2 over the break

plan.do: Class slide 1. Beans, 7 cups, whiteboard, 5 blank cards and her Monday triangle cards. Ask about last night's Show What You Know.
Class slide 2. How Hiccup has changed, what Toothless wants, a sentence that shows another Viking's feelings; every answer backed with a detail.
Class slide 3. Quiz each other with the Monday triangle cards, then the three review items.
Class slide 4. She reads each card and uses it outside math; she finds the opposites surplus and scarce.
Class slides 5–6. Four index cards for 6, 8, 48; she discovers 7, 7, 49 has only two facts.
Class slides 7–8. Pick the family member; decide in or out for the 6, 9, 54 family and say why.
Class slides 9–11. Deal 30 beans into 7 cups; fix Fishlegs' 38 ÷ 6 = 5 R 8 with beans; predict then build 26 ÷ 6.
Class slides 12–13. Which fact fits, how many left, is the remainder smaller than the divisor; say the five steps before tapping.
Class slides 14–15. Clue words and one sentence with surplus and remainder; then three exit-ticket items on her own. Note any miss for Thursday.

Class slide 16. Walk through the two-night task list on the course page: tonight the After-class lesson and Lesson 10 Practice; Wednesday the Lesson 9 Practice, Lesson 9 Packet and Lesson 10 Packet page 1; reading both nights.

watch: Writing backward division facts (6 ÷ 54 = 9) in a family. Say: the top of the triangle comes first in division.
Counting 8 × 9 and 9 × 8 as two different families, or writing 4 facts for 7, 7, 49. Have her write them and see the repeats.
Going over: choosing 7 × 5 = 35 for 30 ÷ 7. Ask: did you use more fish than you have?
A remainder as big as the divisor (38 ÷ 6 = 5 R 8). Ask: could every dragon get one more?
Forgetting the remainder and writing just the quotient. Ask: where did the leftover fish go?
Shutting down on a bigger number. Ask: which fact do you know that is close? Then wait for her.

packet_key.answer: fact family → related facts made from the same three numbers; remainder → the amount left over after dividing; evenly → in equal parts, nothing left over; surplus → an extra amount, more than needed; scarce → hard to find, very little of it; hesitate → to stop for a moment because you are unsure
3 groups of 7 circled with 2 dots left; 23 ÷ 7 = 3 R 2
53 ÷ 9 = 5 R 8: 5 shields on each ship, 8 left over (9 × 5 = 45, 53 − 45 = 8)
Sentences that use surplus (extra amount) and remainder (amount left over after dividing) correctly.
Answers vary; a character from the book, what made them stop and why, using hesitate correctly.

teacher.notes: Bailey takes Show What You Know on her own tonight at the end of the After-class lesson. Check her score before Thursday. If it is under 90, start Thursday with the bean leftovers again (32 ÷ 6, 25 ÷ 8) and one fact family card set, then have her retake (she gets a brand-new question set) before the Lesson 11 class lesson. If the remainder questions are the misses, reteach briefly; remainders come back in full in Week 7. This is the heavy homework stretch: two nights, including Monday's practice and packet.

tasks: Tuesday night: do the After-class lesson. It ends with Show What You Know. You need 90.
Tuesday night: do the Lesson 10 Practice.
Wednesday: print the Lesson 9 Packet and do both pages.
Wednesday: print the Lesson 10 Packet and do page 1 only. Save page 2 for the break.
Tuesday and Wednesday: read How to Train Your Dragon for 15 minutes each night. Look for a moment when a character has to hesitate.

slides.title: Fact Families and Leftovers
slides.text: Yesterday you learned that division undoes multiplication. Today three numbers make a whole family of four facts. Then you find out what happens when things do not share evenly.

notes.do: Set out before she sits down: about 50 dried beans, 7 cups, whiteboard and marker, 5 blank index cards, and ask her to bring her three triangle cards from Monday.
notes.say: "Monday you learned the big idea: division asks a multiplication question. Today you get two new tools: fact families, and what to do with leftovers."
notes.ask: "How did Show What You Know go last night? Which question surprised you?" (Check her Formspree score before class.)

slides.title: Characters on Berk
slides.text: Think about How to Train Your Dragon.
prompts: How has Hiccup changed since the start of the book? Give one example.
What does Toothless want? Does Hiccup want the same thing? How does that cause conflict?
Read me one sentence that shows how another Viking feels about Hiccup. What words give the feeling away?
starters: At the start, Hiccup … but now …

notes.do: 7 minutes. She keeps the book open and finds the sentence for the third prompt herself.
notes.ask: "How has Hiccup changed? Give one example from early in the book and one from now." "What does Toothless want? Is that the same as what Hiccup wants?"
notes.listen: Every answer backed by a detail from the book. If she gives an opinion only, ask: "What happened that makes you think so?"

items.q: What number is hiding in this fact triangle? Type it.
items.no: Ask: 8 × what = 72?

items.q: In 56 ÷ 8 = 7, what is the 8 called?
items.why: The divisor is the number you divide by.
no: The dividend is 56, the number being divided.
The quotient is 7, the answer.

items.q: Stoick packed provisions for the trip. Then he had to ration them. What happened?
choices: He gave out the supplies in small amounts so they would last.
He ate everything on the first day.
items.why: Provisions are packed supplies; to ration is to give them out in small, set amounts.
no: Rationing keeps supplies, it does not throw them away.
That is the opposite of rationing.
Rationing means making what you have last longer.

notes.do: Before the slide, 2 minutes with her Monday triangle cards: she quizzes you on one, then you quiz her on two.
notes.ask: "Say the multiplication question for the triangle before you type."
notes.listen: She should still say "8 times what is 72" without prompting. If not, spend one more minute on it before new material.

slides.title: Words for today
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Read it out loud. Then tell me where you could use the word outside of math.

words.meaning: A set of related multiplication and division facts made from the same three numbers.
The amount left over when a number cannot be split into equal groups.
In equal parts, with nothing left over.
An extra amount, more than what is needed.
words.example: After every dragon was fed, there was a surplus of 3 fish.

words.meaning: Hard to find because there is very little of it.
words.example: In the middle of winter, fresh food was scarce.

words.meaning: To stop or wait for a moment before doing something, because you are unsure.
words.example: Do not hesitate: if you know 7 × 8 = 56, you know 56 ÷ 8.

words.meaning: To talk with someone to reach an agreement.
words.example: Instead of fighting, the two tribes agreed to negotiate.

notes.do: She reads each card aloud and gives a use outside math. Write fact family and remainder on the whiteboard; you will add to them later.
notes.say: "Two math words, five story words. Two of the story words are opposites. Find them." (surplus and scarce.)
notes.ask: "Use hesitate about a moment in your book." "When would two Viking tribes negotiate instead of fight?" "What would a surplus of fish look like on our cups?"
notes.listen: Surplus = extra, scarce = very little. For evenly, she must say "nothing left over", not just "equal".

slides.title: Three numbers, four facts
slides.text: The numbers 6, 8 and 48 make a fact family. From one triangle you get four facts.
slides.tip: In both division facts, the biggest number (the top of the triangle) comes first.

notes.do: Hands-on: she writes the four facts for 6, 8, 48 on four blank index cards, one fact per card, and lines them up under her triangle.
notes.ask: Before each step: "What is the next fact in the family?" After all four: "Which number starts both division facts? Why?"
notes.listen: "48 comes first because it is the total, the biggest number."

slides.title: A family with only two facts
slides.text: Look at the numbers 7, 7 and 49. Try to write four facts.

steps.text: So the 7, 7, 49 family has only 2 different facts.

slides.tip: When the two bottom numbers are the same, the family has 2 facts, not 4.

notes.do: Give her a blank card: "Write the 7, 7, 49 family." Let her discover the repeats before you reveal the steps.
notes.ask: "Look at your four cards. Are any of them exactly the same?" "Which other families would only have two facts?" (6, 6, 36; 8, 8, 64; 9, 9, 81.)
notes.listen: She explains WHY: the turn-around of 7 × 7 is itself.

items.q: Which fact belongs in the same family as 9 × 7 = 63?
items.why: 63 ÷ 9 = 7 uses the same three numbers: 7, 9 and 63.
no: Subtraction facts are not in a multiplication and division family.
Backward! The biggest number must come first in division.
That fact uses 8 and 72, not 7 and 63.

items.no: Which number is not used yet in the division facts?

items.q: Which list is a complete fact family?
items.why: All four facts use only 8, 9 and 72.
no: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 is true, but 6 and 12 are not in this family.
9 ÷ 72 is backward, and adding is not in the family.
81 is a different family.

notes.say: "A fact belongs only if it uses the same three numbers AND it is true."
notes.ask: For every wrong choice she rejects: "Why doesn't it belong?"
notes.listen: Three reasons a fact does not belong: wrong numbers, backward division, or the wrong operation (+ or −).

slides.title: In or out of the 6, 9, 54 family?
slides.text: Type in or out. Then say why.

items.q: 54 ÷ 6 = 8.   Is it in or out?
items.why: 6 × 8 = 48, not 54. A false fact is not in any family.
items.no: Check it: 6 × 8 = ?

items.q: 6 ÷ 54 = 9.   Is it in or out?
items.why: Backward. In division the biggest number comes first.
items.no: Which number should come first in division?

items.q: 9 × 6 = 54.   Is it in or out?
items.why: The turn-around fact uses the same three numbers, and it is true.
items.no: Same three numbers? True?

items.q: 45 ÷ 9 = 5.   Is it in or out?
items.why: 45 is not 54. The digits got switched.
items.no: Read the first number carefully: 45 or 54?

notes.do: She can lay her 6, 9, 54 triangle card next to the screen while she decides.
notes.ask: "Why?" after every answer, even the right ones.
notes.listen: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 is the trap: it is a true fact but uses different numbers. Praise her if she catches the switched digits.

slides.title: When it does not share evenly
slides.text: Hiccup has 30 fish for 7 dragons. Every dragon must get the same number. How many does each dragon get?

visual.sub: Every dragon gets the same number.

steps.text: Ask: 7 × what gets close to 30 without going over?
30 − 28 = 2 fish left over. That is the remainder.

visual.label: 7 dragons, 4 fish each: 28 fish. 2 fish are left over.

slides.tip: The remainder must be smaller than the divisor. If 7 or more were left over, every dragon could get one more fish!

notes.do: Hands-on first, slide second: give her 30 beans and 7 cups. She deals one bean per cup per round until she cannot do a full round. Then reveal the steps.
notes.ask: "How many in each cup?" (4). "How many in your hand?" (2). "Why can't the 2 go in?" (Not enough for every cup.) "Which fact did your rounds make?" (7 × 4 = 28.)
notes.listen: "There aren't enough for every dragon to get one more." That sentence is the whole idea of a remainder.

slides.title: Too many left? One more group fits!
slides.text: Fishlegs tried 38 ÷ 6. He wrote 5 R 8. Find his mistake.

steps.text: But 8 is bigger than 6. Every group can get one more!

slides.tip: Always ask: is my remainder smaller than the divisor?

notes.do: She builds it: 38 beans, 6 cups, but she stops after 5 rounds like Fishlegs. Then she looks at the 8 beans in her hand.
notes.ask: "Can every cup get one more bean?" (Yes, 8 is at least 6.) "So was 5 the biggest fact that fits?"
notes.listen: She connects "leftover too big" with "I picked a fact that was too small".

slides.title: Dinner for six dragons
slides.text: Hiccup has 26 fish and 6 dragons. Give every dragon the same number of fish, as many as you can. Make the groups.
slides.why: 6 × 4 = 24 fish handed out. 26 − 24 = 2 left over. So 26 ÷ 6 = 4 R 2.
slides.hint: 6 dragons means 6 groups. Is 6 × 5 = 30 more than 26? Then each dragon gets fewer than 5.

notes.do: She predicts the answer with a fact first (6 × 4 = 24, 2 left), then sets the counters. Beans only if her prediction is wrong.
notes.ask: "Which 6s fact is the biggest that fits under 26?"
notes.listen: She rejects 6 × 5 = 30 because it is over 26.

slides.title: Leftovers
slides.text: Type the answer with R for the remainder, like 4 R 2.

items.no: Find the biggest 7s fact that fits under 45 without going over.

items.q: Fishlegs says 50 ÷ 9 = 4 R 14. What is wrong?
choices: 14 left over is enough for one more group of 9. It should be 5 R 5.
no: The math adds up, but a remainder can never be as big as the divisor.
9 × 5 = 45, so 5 are left over, not 0.

items.q: Which division has no remainder?
items.why: 9 × 7 = 63 exactly, so nothing is left over.
no: 8 × 6 = 48, so 4 are left over.
6 × 7 = 42, so 1 is left over.
7 × 8 = 56, so 4 are left over.

notes.do: She works on the whiteboard first, then types.
notes.say: "Three questions for every leftover problem: which fact fits, how many are left, is the remainder smaller than the divisor?"
notes.listen: On 45 ÷ 7 she should reject 7 × 7 = 49 (over) and pick 7 × 6 = 42.

slides.title: Steps for 50 ÷ 8
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
steps: Ask: 8 × what gets close to 50 without going over?
Check: 2 is smaller than 8, so no more groups fit
slides.why: Find the biggest fact that fits, subtract, check the remainder, then write it.
slides.hint: You can't subtract until you know which fact fits. What comes first?

notes.do: She says all five steps out loud from memory BEFORE tapping. Then she taps.
notes.ask: "Why do we check that 2 is smaller than 8?"
notes.listen: Find the fact, subtract, check, write. Those four words are what you want her to keep.

items.q: The amount left over after dividing is called the ____.
items.why: The remainder is the part left over.
items.no: It starts with r. On paper we write just its first letter.

items.q: Fresh water was scarce on the long voyage. What does that tell you?
choices: There was a surplus of water.
items.why: Scarce means hard to find because there is very little.
no: A surplus is extra. Scarce is the opposite.
Scarce tells how much, not how it tastes.
Scarce does not tell how it was shared.

items.q: Hiccup hesitated at the edge of the cliff. Which word means the opposite of hesitated?
items.why: To hesitate is to stop for a moment; rushing ahead is the opposite.
no: Paused means almost the same as hesitated.
Worry might be why he hesitated, but it is not the opposite.
Looking down is a different action, not the opposite.

notes.ask: "What clue word helped?" Then: "Use surplus and remainder in one sentence about our beans."
notes.listen: Something like: "We had a surplus of 2 beans, which was the remainder."

slides.title: Show me before you go
slides.text: On your own. No help this time.

items.no: Which number is not used yet?
Find the biggest 8s fact that fits under 35 without going over.

items.q: How many different facts are in the 9, 9, 81 family? Type a number.
items.why: 9 × 9 = 81 and 81 ÷ 9 = 9. The turn-arounds are the same facts.
items.no: Write them. Are any the same?

notes.do: She types these herself. Do not help. Note what she misses: that is where to start Thursday.
notes.listen: If she misses the remainder item, she does the after-class lesson tonight anyway; the leftovers slide there reminds her of the steps.
